artists.biography:
Porcupine Tree are a rock band formed by Steven Wilson in 1987 in Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire, England. Their music is associated with both psychedelic rock and progressive rock, yet having been influenced by trance, krautrock and ambient due to Steven Wilson and Richard Barbieri's penchant for the Kosmische Musik scene of the early 1970s, led by bands such as Tangerine Dream, Neu! and Can. Since the early 2000s (decade), their music has been leaning towards progressive metal and alternative rock.
The band is noted for its multimedia approach, with its live performances including screens displaying a different film projection to each song. This visual element was introduced during the tour for the In Absentia album, when the band started to work with Danish photographer and filmmaker Lasse Hoile. This involvement created a distinctive image for the band.
Despite being signed to both Roadrunner and Atlantic labels, the band has their own record label, Transmission, which they use to launch some independent releases and special editions of their albums. In 2007 the band was nominated for a Grammy Award for Best Surround Sound Album with their album Fear of a Blank Planet and then again in 2010 with The Incident.
Music Radar website placed them amongst "The 30 greatest live acts in the world today" (as of 2010), coming at number 4.

perplexity.description:
The Delerium Years 1991–1993" is a compilation box set by Porcupine Tree, originally released in 2017, that gathers the band's earliest recordings from their formative years on the Delerium label. Musically, the set showcases Porcupine Tree's roots in psychedelic rock, space rock, and progressive rock, reflecting the experimental and atmospheric sound that defined their initial output. The collection includes the studio albums On the Sunday of Life... and Up the Downstair, along with rare tracks and mini-albums such as Staircase Infinities, offering a comprehensive look at the band's evolution from a studio project into a full-fledged group.

This box set holds a significant place in Porcupine Tree's discography as it documents the period when Steven Wilson and his collaborators established the sonic identity that would later influence their more widely recognized progressive rock style. While the original albums were initially released to a niche audience within the UK underground scene, "The Delerium Years 1991–1993" brought renewed attention to these foundational works, allowing both longtime fans and new listeners to appreciate the band's early experimentation. The set was well-received for its historical value and the quality of its remastered audio, though it was not a commercial release in the traditional sense but rather a retrospective collection that underscored Porcupine Tree's enduring legacy in the rock genre.
